# S3

Store object metadata in the shared store and object/version/multipart bytes in local files.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `s3` |
| Signing name | `s3` |
| Wire protocol | REST XML |
| API version | `2006-03-01` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Local behavior |
| Selected operations | 90 of 112 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#s3) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Encryption settings are metadata; objects are not encrypted as an AWS S3 data plane would encrypt them, and writes asking for aws:kms are accepted and stored like AES256 objects (aws:kms:dsse is rejected).
- General ACL evaluation is unsupported. Resource policies do not govern in-process reads.
- POST form fields other than key, Content-Type, x-amz-meta-*, Object Lock, success_action_* and signature fields (acl, tagging, storage class, encryption, cache headers) return NotImplemented; SigV2 POST signatures are unsupported.
- Generated in-process PutObject/UploadPart byte-slice shapes, in-process reads (e.g. Lambda runtime Object() helper), and console download and preview buffers still buffer bytes in memory.
- Verify mode spools signed hexadecimal or missing payload hashes to temporary files. Supported aws-chunked modes stream directly and verify mode checks each signed chunk, the terminator, and signed trailers.
- Console uploads are limited to 1 MiB per file; object browsing and management in verify mode require an authenticated root console session; storage.s3_max_object_bytes defaults to 256 MiB and can be set up to 5 GiB for object PUTs, parts and completed multipart objects.
- Access log batches are bounded. Best-effort delivery can drop records during overload or after a batch has been claimed. Destination grants are stored without ACL enforcement.
- Analytics and inventory reports, request metrics, and automatic Intelligent-Tiering moves are not produced. Acceleration and request payment are settings only, with no accelerated transfer or billing.
- Replication does not backfill existing objects or synchronize version deletions or metadata changes. The role ARN identifies the replication principal for destination policy evaluation. Role assumption, role policy execution, and replication time control are unsupported.
- Restore timing is simulated. Archive retrieval is available for transitioned or replicated versions. Direct writes accept STANDARD storage only, and restore notifications are unsupported.
- SSE-C simulates key validation. Object files remain plaintext. Multipart destination encryption and SSE-C for browser POST are unsupported.
- GetObjectAttributes omits ObjectParts for nonmultipart objects and objects completed before part metadata was retained.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
